regions.merged_text: God bless you Muriel Krausman and many thanks for favor of June 6th. I am glad you are feelin not too bad-like myself-battling along one day at a time .... Had a solemn high Mass today - 35th anniversary of my Brother Maurice Joachim's first Mass Celebration. That was in Superior, Wisconsin 1911. Thanks be to God. He is in St. Paul, Minn. now with our Rt. Rev. Br. Edw'd back from the Philippines. Latter was rescued last year, March 23rd. Will be going back before long. It would seem that the Japps had been figuering on a general massacre of the whole camp - that day - over two thousand, including two Bishops, 150 priests and 125 nuns. They ( the prisoners) had been saying the holy rosary and having Bene- diction every day and Pontifical Mass every Sunday that they might be res- cued without anything too drastic. Most of the prisoners were so starved that they could hardly walk. About 20 actually died of malnutrition - starved. . . .
